hpi: {{patient_name}} is a 28-year-old man with gross hematuria, bilateral flank pain, and hypertension on repeat clinic readings. Exam shows palpable bilateral flank fullness. His father has autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD). ADPKD is the most common inherited kidney disease — mutations in PKD1 (85%, chromosome 16) or PKD2 (15%, chromosome 4). Cysts develop in kidneys (and liver, pancreas) over decades, eventually causing renal failure by age 50-60. Diagnosis: renal ultrasound — multiple bilateral cysts in enlarged kidneys (usually by age 30 for PKD1). CT/MRI for more detail. Labs: elevated Cr (declining renal function), UA shows hematuria. Screen for cerebral aneurysms (berry aneurysms — 5-10% of ADPKD patients, higher if family history) with MRA/CTA brain. Management: BP control with ACEI/ARB (nephroprotective), treat UTIs aggressively, avoid contact sports (cyst rupture risk). Tolvaptan (vasopressin antagonist) slows cyst growth. Genetic counseling.
